subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC: data isolation expectations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finsecure.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and can get you the right materials: 

Summary of your requirements we captured:
- Primary concern: strict data isolation and control for customer PII and financial transaction logs.
- Regulatory drivers: SOC 2 + upcoming audit, need for customer-managed keying and limited admin access.
- Traffic: estimated steady-state inference volume ~500k tokens/day with periodic spikes during batch scoring.
- Decision drivers: whether to use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our tenancy) vs Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem deployment) — key question is isolation boundaries and auditability.

Short answers (we'll follow up with technical doc attached):
- Dedicated: provides isolated capacity (dedicated GPU pools) and logical isolation at the service level; metadata/metrics and control plane are still hosted by Redwood. Good for predictable throughput and lower TCO vs on-prem, but customers who require network-level isolation or their own VPC typically choose Private.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): brings the control plane and/or runtime into your VPC or on-prem environment (options vary by contract). Allows for customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM for encryption keys, and stricter egress/firewall controls.

Open questions we captured for your infra/security team (please confirm):
1) Do you require customer-managed KMS for model/data encryption at rest?
2) Are outbound network policies required to prevent any egress to third-party infra?
3) Do you need access to raw request/response logs for retention in your SIEM, or are structured audit logs sufficient?

Next steps:
- I'm attaching a short data isolation overview and our SOC 2 summary (stubbed attachments).
- I'll loop in Mateo (solutions) to answer the technical KMS/VPC questions — can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week for infra alignment?
- If you prefer, we can kick off a Private deployment checklist review to surface any nonstandard requirements.

Attachments: redwood-data-isolation-overview.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. Short answers to your open questions: 
1) Yes, customer-managed KMS is required for any production deployment touching PII.
2) Yes, we cannot have any uncontrolled outbound egress from the inference runtime. All traffic must go through our monitored egress and proxy.
3) We need request/response logs forwarded to our SIEM for 180-day retention — structured audit logs alone won't be sufficient for the audit team.

Given those constraints, we're leaning toward Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Two quick asks before we schedule the infra call: 
- Can you confirm whether Dedicated includes the option for customer-managed KMS or whether that's Private-only?
- Do you have an example network diagram for the Private VPC deployment (peering vs transit gateway options)?

Appreciate the SOC2 doc — could you also share any architecture guidance and the private-deployment-checklist you mentioned?

Best,
Alice Johnson
Director of Infrastructure | FinSecure
alice@finsecure.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@finsecure.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick clarity. Mateo is on this thread to answer the technical specifics; answers below at a high level while Mateo confirms exact operational details: 

- Customer-managed KMS: Private deployments fully support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated, we offer envelope encryption where you can provide keys in some enterprise agreements, but full customer-managed key residency is typically only available with Private (VPC/on-prem) due to control plane constraints. I'll flag that as a contractual item.
- Network/egress: Private lets you place the runtime inside your VPC or on-prem so all outbound traffic obeys your egress controls. With Dedicated, we can restrict egress to a whitelist but the runtime remains in Redwood's network fabric.
- Logs: For Private we can ship raw request/response logs to your SIEM, or you can host a collector in your VPC. For Dedicated we provide structured audit logs and aggregated metrics — raw payloads are only available under strict DPA terms.

I've attached our private-deployment-checklist.xlsx and an architecture diagram link for VPC peering vs TGW.

Proposed next steps:
- Mateo, can you confirm KMS options and whether we can support customer-provided keys under a Dedicated contract (or if that requires Private)?
- Alice/Bob, does Tuesday 6/15 10:00am PT work for a 30-min infra call? If not, propose two slots and I'll coordinate.

Attachments: private-deployment-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alice / Marissa — Mateo here (Solutions). Quick technical answers and confirmations to unblock the infra check: 

1) KMS/HSM: Private (VPC/on-prem) supports full customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMKs or on-prem HSM). For Dedicated, we support envelope encryption where you can provide a key material reference; however, Dedicated tenants still require some control-plane interactions with Redwood-managed services. If you require strict key residency with no Redwood control-plane access to key material, Private is the recommended path.

2) Network/egress: With Private VPC we support both VPC peering and Transit Gateway (TGW) topologies. The runtime can be deployed inside your VPC subnets so outbound egress follows your routing/NAT configuration. We can also deploy a collector sidecar for log forwarding into your private collectors. For Dedicated, egress can be limited to a whitelist but the runtime exits our network fabric.

3) Logs: Private supports forwarding full request/response payloads to your SIEM or S3 bucket (customer-managed); we can also provide signed delivery or in-VPC collectors. For Dedicated we provide structured audit logs and token-level metrics; raw payload export is possible but requires DPA addendum and strict controls.

Operational notes:
- Admin access: Private gives you the ability to use your IdP and RBAC within the VPC runtime. Dedicated has RBAC at the account level but limited node-level control.
- Patch/updates: We provide a maintenance window model; for Private on-prem installs we can provide signed releases and a controlled maintenance cadence.

Next steps I suggest:
- Share a draft network diagram (I attached our VPC peer/TGW examples link) and we'll mark required ports and CIDRs.
- Let's schedule a 30-min infra sync where we'll include one of our security engineers. Marissa — can you confirm Tuesday 6/15 10:00am PT?

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (copy), private-deployment-checklist.xlsx (copy)
